subject: Nimble for multiple dataset on same model

messages.author: 697cdfacf5b0f418
messages.subject: Nimble for multiple dataset on same model
parts:
Hi Nimble experts,

I have to run some simulation datasets using the same model, and I am wondering if we can create a loop to make things easier or if we need to use compile_model$setData for specific datasets every time. Please see the code below, I appreciate any insights and suggestions. 

Icar.model<-nimbleCode({
 
  for (i in 1:N){
    rw[i]~dbinom(pw[i],tn[i])
   
    logit(pw[i])<-betaw+u1[i]
   
    lb[i]~dbinom(pb[i],tn[i])
   
    logit(pb[i])<-betab+u2[i]
   
   
    prow[i]<-exp(betaw+u1[i])/(1+exp(betaw+u1[i]))
    prob[i]<-exp(betab+u2[i])/(1+exp(betab+u2[i]))
   
    index[i]<-prow[i]-prob[i]
   
   
  }
 
  u1[1:N]~dcar_normal(adj[1:L], weights[1:L], num[1:N], tau1, zero_mean = 1)
  u2[1:N]~dcar_normal(adj[1:L], weights[1:L], num[1:N], tau2, zero_mean = 1)
 
 
  betaw~dnorm(0,10000)
  betab~dnorm(0,10000)
 
  #tau~dgamma(1,0.01)
  tau1~dgamma(0.1,0.001)
  sigma2.tau1 <- 1/tau1
  tau2~dgamma(0.1,0.001)
  sigma2.tau2 <- 1/tau2
})

Inits1<-list(tau1=0.1,tau2=0.1, pw=rep(0.1, 159),pb=rep(0.1,159),
             betaw=1 , betab=1, u1=rep(0.1,159),u2=rep(0.1,159))

Model.icar<-nimbleModel(code=Icar.model, constants=constant,
                        data=list(rw=sim$w1,
                                  lb=sim$b1), inits=Inits1). ----sim$w1 indicates simulation dataset 1

CModel.icar<-compileNimble(Model.icar)
LCModel.icar<-configureMCMC(Model.icar,print=TRUE,enableWAIC=TRUE,
                            monitors=CModel.icar$getNodeNames(stochOnly=TRUE,
                                                        includeData=FALSE))

LCModel.icar$addMonitors(c("index"))  
Model.icarMCMC<-buildMCMC(LCModel.icar)
CModel.icarMCMC<-compileNimble(Model.icarMCMC,project=Model.icar)
niter<-200000
set.seed(234546)
samples1.icar<-runMCMC(CModel.icarMCMC,niter=niter,nburnin=150000,nchains=1,thin=100)

CModel.icar$setData(list(rw=sim$w2,lb=sim$b2)) ----running simulation dataset 2
samples2.icar<-runMCMC(CModel.icarMCMC,niter=niter,nburnin=150000,nchains=1,thin=100)

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Nimble for multiple dataset on same model
parts:
Hi Bill,

Thanks for the question.

You can also change the data values by simple assignment:

CModel.icar$rw <- sim$w2
CModel.icar$b2 <- sim$b2

(In fact, the setData method is really most appropriate for an uncompiled model before creating an MCMC.  At that step, setData both assigns values and flags those nodes as data nodes.  The data flags are then used by configureMCMC and/or buildMCMC.  If you use setData later from the compiled model, as your code does, it will assign the data values, but it is too late to change which nodes are flagged as data, so that will not be done.  Therefore, you might as well simply assign values without calling setData.)

If your question is whether there is any way to not do a new MCMC run for each new dataset: No, you need a new MCMC run for each.

HTH.

Perry

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: Nimble for multiple dataset on same model
parts:
Yes, you can do this. Just follow the approach in our parallelization example , but with a change along the following lines:

```
run_MCMC_allcode <- function(idx, data, code, useWAIC = TRUE) {
  library(nimble)
 
  myModel <- nimbleModel(code = code,
                          data = list(y = data[[idx]]),
                          constants = list(length_y = 1000),
                          inits = list(a = 0.5, b = 0.5))
CmyModel <- compileNimble(myModel)

  if(useWAIC)
    monitors <- myModel$getParents(myModel$getNodeNames(dataOnly = TRUE), stochOnly = TRUE)
  ## One may also wish to add additional monitors
 
  myMCMC <- buildMCMC(CmyModel, monitors = monitors)
  CmyMCMC <- compileNimble(myMCMC)
 
  results <- runMCMC(CmyMCMC, niter = 10000, setSeed = idx)
 
  return(results)
}
```

You'll need `data` to be a list, with each element being a list of data for a given dataset you want to fit.

-chris

I saw the example on https://r-nimble.org/nimbleExamples/parallelizing_NIMBLE.html, but still not sure how to apply that approach when we have different datasets (thought they have the same size).

Thanks~

On Monday, October 31, 2022 at 2:31:58 PM UTC-4 Perry de Valpine wrote:
Hi Bill,

Thanks for the question.

You can also change the data values by simple assignment:

CModel.icar$rw <- sim$w2
CModel.icar$b2 <- sim$b2

(In fact, the setData method is really most appropriate for an uncompiled model before creating an MCMC.  At that step, setData both assigns values and flags those nodes as data nodes.  The data flags are then used by configureMCMC and/or buildMCMC.  If you use setData later from the compiled model, as your code does, it will assign the data values, but it is too late to change which nodes are flagged as data, so that will not be done.  Therefore, you might as well simply assign values without calling setData.)

If your question is whether there is any way to not do a new MCMC run for each new dataset: No, you need a new MCMC run for each.

HTH.

Perry

On Mon, Oct 31, 2022 at 7:19 AM Bill Chen <billchen...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Nimble experts,

I have to run some simulation datasets using the same model, and I am wondering if we can create a loop to make things easier or if we need to use compile_model$setData for specific datasets every time. Please see the code below, I appreciate any insights and suggestions. 

Icar.model<-nimbleCode({
 
  for (i in 1:N){
    rw[i]~dbinom(pw[i],tn[i])
   
    logit(pw[i])<-betaw+u1[i]
   
    lb[i]~dbinom(pb[i],tn[i])
   
    logit(pb[i])<-betab+u2[i]
   
   
    prow[i]<-exp(betaw+u1[i])/(1+exp(betaw+u1[i]))
    prob[i]<-exp(betab+u2[i])/(1+exp(betab+u2[i]))
   
    index[i]<-prow[i]-prob[i]
   
   
  }
 
  u1[1:N]~dcar_normal(adj[1:L], weights[1:L], num[1:N], tau1, zero_mean = 1)
  u2[1:N]~dcar_normal(adj[1:L], weights[1:L], num[1:N], tau2, zero_mean = 1)
 
 
  betaw~dnorm(0,10000)
  betab~dnorm(0,10000)
 
  #tau~dgamma(1,0.01)
  tau1~dgamma(0.1,0.001)
  sigma2.tau1 <- 1/tau1
  tau2~dgamma(0.1,0.001)
  sigma2.tau2 <- 1/tau2
})

Inits1<-list(tau1=0.1,tau2=0.1, pw=rep(0.1, 159),pb=rep(0.1,159),
             betaw=1 , betab=1, u1=rep(0.1,159),u2=rep(0.1,159))

Model.icar<-nimbleModel(code=Icar.model, constants=constant,
                        data=list(rw=sim$w1,
                                  lb=sim$b1), inits=Inits1). ----sim$w1 indicates simulation dataset 1

CModel.icar<-compileNimble(Model.icar)
LCModel.icar<-configureMCMC(Model.icar,print=TRUE,enableWAIC=TRUE,
                            monitors=CModel.icar$getNodeNames(stochOnly=TRUE,
                                                        includeData=FALSE))

LCModel.icar$addMonitors(c("index"))  
Model.icarMCMC<-buildMCMC(LCModel.icar)
CModel.icarMCMC<-compileNimble(Model.icarMCMC,project=Model.icar)
niter<-200000
set.seed(234546)
samples1.icar<-runMCMC(CModel.icarMCMC,niter=niter,nburnin=150000,nchains=1,thin=100)

CModel.icar$setData(list(rw=sim$w2,lb=sim$b2)) ----running simulation dataset 2
samples2.icar<-runMCMC(CModel.icarMCMC,niter=niter,nburnin=150000,nchains=1,thin=100)

On Thursday, December 21, 2023 at 1:05:43 PM UTC-5 Chris Paciorek wrote:
Yes, you can do this. Just follow the approach in our parallelization example , but with a change along the following lines:

```
run_MCMC_allcode <- function(idx, data, code, useWAIC = TRUE) {
  library(nimble)
 
  myModel <- nimbleModel(code = code,
                          data = list(y = data[[idx]]),
                          constants = list(length_y = 1000),
                          inits = list(a = 0.5, b = 0.5))
CmyModel <- compileNimble(myModel)

  if(useWAIC)
    monitors <- myModel$getParents(myModel$getNodeNames(dataOnly = TRUE), stochOnly = TRUE)
  ## One may also wish to add additional monitors
 
  myMCMC <- buildMCMC(CmyModel, monitors = monitors)
  CmyMCMC <- compileNimble(myMCMC)
 
  results <- runMCMC(CmyMCMC, niter = 10000, setSeed = idx)
 
  return(results)
}
```

You'll need `data` to be a list, with each element being a list of data for a given dataset you want to fit.

-chris

Sorry that I may not be clear.  In my case, I want to fit the same Poisson Gaussian process model. I said the same because the prior is the same, the initial values are the same, and the likelihood function is the same. The only difference is that the data to be fit are different. I thought I could utilize parallelization, e.g., on thread 1 we fit the model for dataset 1, in thread 2 we fit the model for dataset 2, and so on.
Could I use parallelization in this case?

Thanks!

On Tuesday, December 19, 2023 at 5:01:29 PM UTC-5 Perry de Valpine wrote:
Hi Juan,
Yes, you could parallelize, but since each thread needs to build and compile its own model, the workflow would not be much different than simply parallelizing and using different data in each thread. There wouldn't be a way to re-use the model across threads, if that's what you're wondering about. I might not have grasped the question, so feel free to clarify.
Perry
